records.title: Has Louisiana availability become observed broadband adoption?
records.decision: Accept the named-cohort answer; reject transfer to broader adoption claims
records.rationale: The complete answer and three sections correctly distinguish service availability from observed subscriptions. The exact 104-location Bossier cohort is not the statewide 7,460-location award, provider-wide subscriber base or Starlink cohort. The September 22 source note additionally separates the tower location in Bienville Parish from the served cohort. The retained September 10 receipt supports this bounded conclusion without a new adoption gate decision. No take rate or zero-subscriber observation is warranted.

findings.finding: A tower in Bienville Parish can be discussed separately from the named Bossier service cohort. Preserve that distinction in source notes and do not move the cohort or combine provider identities.

Keep fixed eligible locations, observed subscriptions, period and method together before calculating adoption. Availability checkers, construction forecasts and broad company totals cannot fill the numerator.

This does not resolve the broader historical human-futures research question or every Louisiana provider. Replace the current pending-human editorial label only through the new AI-review projection; retain original wording as history.
